question: Can independently mapped wetland context be assigned to enough NAAMP physical listening sites to test whether rainfall recruitment depends on wetland hydrology?
population: Unique SiteID values used by the frozen 4,236 matched NAAMP wetter-drier pairs.

sources.wetlands: Official U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service National Wetlands Inventory Wetlands MapServer layer 0.

spatial_linkage.rule: For each SiteID, choose the nearest NWI polygon. A site is classified at a radius only when nearest polygon distance is <= that radius. Distance is computed in a route-centered local azimuthal equidistant projection.
spatial_linkage.multiple_polygons: Nearest polygon wins; ties within 1 m are reported as ambiguous rather than outcome-selected.
spatial_linkage.rationale: NAAMP wetland-associated stops were selected near potential wetland habitat; prior NAAMP landscape work describes water bodies visible within 200 m of the road.

feasibility_gate.site_coverage_primary: >= 0.50 of pair-used SiteIDs have a nearest NWI polygon within 200 m
feasibility_gate.hydrology_field_coverage: >= 0.80 of primary-matched sites have nonempty WATER_REGIME_NAME
feasibility_gate.variation: At least two WATER_REGIME_NAME categories each contain >=250 unique matched SiteIDs.
feasibility_gate.consequence_if_fail: Do not use NWI water regime as the primary measured-context mechanism test; retain it only as descriptive context.

interpretation_boundary: NWI is mapped wetland habitat, not water level on the NAAMP survey night.
NWI mapping dates can differ from NAAMP survey dates.
A nearby NWI polygon does not prove that the detected frog called from that polygon.
This eligibility audit does not inspect frog-response endpoints.
